The Wonder

There is a more known tune, called “The Wonder”, but in Central Connecticut where I attend sessions, this “The Wonder” is a lot more known. We play this after another hornpipe, “Fairy Queen.” Does anyone know the background of this tune? I would love to know!

This is a strange setting, I think your tune changed names somewhere along the line. “The Wonder” that I’ve always heard is the other setting submitted by Joerg.

Looking at this tune I think it is actually a hornpipe called the Ballyoran (composed by Sean Ryan?).

Composer…

Yes, it was composed by Sean Ryan.

The person who taught it to me told me that this tune was submitted to a tune competition (is there such a thing at the All-Ireland?) in the same year as Father Kelly submitted “Father Kelly’s” reel. The “Ballyoran Hornpipe” won, “Father Kelly’s” came in second.

↳ Posted by browndog on October 23rd, 2004.

The Ballyoran Hornpipe

There is a Wonder Hornpipe posted here, which has the name ‘Ballyoran Hornpipe’ in brackets after it, but it sounds like a Reel to me.

Although, one may well have come from the other.

This ‘Hornpipe version’ I got from Gay McKeon’s tape ‘Irish Piping Tradition’ where he says: “The Ballyoran Hornpipe was sourced from my brother’s manuscript of Leo Rowsome tunes.”

↳ Posted by briantheflute on November 25th, 2020.

Re: The Ballyoran

This tune was originally christened “The Wonder Hornpipe” by Fr John Quinn who named a lot of tunes for Ryan. Fr Quinn tells me: “When Seán played this for me for the first time, he said, “isn’t it a wonderful hornpipe?” So straight away I said, “we’ll call it ‘The Wonder Hornpipe’ ”, and that’s the title it had when, with it, “The Glen of Aherlow” and “The Nightingale”, Seán won the first All-Ireland competition for newly composed tunes [in 1960]. Things didn’t rest so, however, and soon it got a different name by which it is now widely known, “The Ballyoran”. And just as well, as there is another older hornpipe called “The Wonder”.”

↳ Posted by ConorW on August 26th, 2023.

↳ Posted by leprecawn on October 24th, 2024.

Re: The Ballyoran

Having listened to numerous musicians playing this hornpipe and a recommendation from a well known authority /lecturer on Traditional Irish music, last four notes in bar 5 changed from printed sheet music of composer ie ABFA to cBAF # being in key of G. It goes against the grain for me to make any alteration if I have the composers original notation , but I have to agree that this small change makes for a nice follow on to the next bar.

↳ Posted by leprecawn on October 27th, 2024.
